answer: Receipts are committed as salted hashes first and revealed only after the epoch closes, so a copycat cannot read the work and resubmit it. A failed audit slashes the bond, and the reviewer must have no shared funding or referral tie with the submitter. Edge case: an honest agent in a small haven of one provider gets flagged, so the inlet rule counts distinct /24s, not /16s. To farm, you need real work behind every hash, and a wander through proxies still shows in the funding graph.
